title: Generation Aesthetics: Zyzz, the Godfather of Terrible Role Models
summary: A long critique of Zyzz and the aesthetic movement he spawned, prompted by his resurgence through YouTube Shorts memes. NH argues Zyzz died from drug abuse rather than bad luck, was small off-cycle, and has been mythified into a fake alpha icon. He says the copycat aesthetic channels who lie about drug use, sell products and promote promiscuity have replaced natural bodybuilding and damage young lifters.
claims: Death doesn't exempt someone from criticism; a bad influence in life remains a bad influence after death
Zyzz's fame was small and divisive while he was alive; the myth snowballed after his death
Zyzz is effectively the father of modern YouTube aesthetics culture
Zyzz died at 22 from steroids, cutting agents, a poor diet and lack of rest, not from bad luck; the congenital heart defect story is too convenient
Almost every bodybuilder who dies of a heart attack is said to have had a congenital condition, which points to the drugs
Excusing a drug user's death as random tells young lifters they bear no responsibility for what they take
YouTube fitness is hypocritical: it praises drug users' physiques, then acts surprised when they die
Zyzz didn't have great genetics; off-cycle he looked small, soft and worse than average
Arnold looked pudgy and ordinary when off drugs for his film career; drug users shrink to normal or mediocre within 3-4 months off
Pros train inefficiently because drugs make anything work, and fans wrongly copy their routines
Zyzz lifted naturally for only about a year before taking drugs, which is nothing in natural bodybuilding, so he never knew how to get there naturally
Bodybuilding.com users refused to give a teenage Zyzz steroid advice because he was too young
Tall lifters have more frame to fill and need more time to build muscle naturally
NH was 110 lb at 6 ft as a teen, a skeleton like the young Zyzz
Zyzz was an insecure gamer who tried to escape his self-hatred through drugs, not a model of masculinity
The internet mythified Zyzz after death into an alpha-male archetype; most of what fans believe about him is projection
Male power fantasies are good, but following one that doesn't actually carry positive values leads you astray
Shorts are the lowest form of content and suit Zyzz memes because he had little substance and rarely spoke on camera
Zyzz was impatient, lazy, couldn't stick to a diet and was a drug addict, the opposite of a role model
A male power fantasy should be someone above you both physically and intellectually
Zyzz's confidence came from drugs, including MDMA and amphetamines; without them he was shy, especially with women
Parasocial relationships grow stronger after the person dies because only a malleable image is left
Copying a strong individual makes you a clone, not an individual
Self-love comes from within; changing only the outside without inner work makes things worse
The only way to change yourself is to work and suffer, since you are both the sculptor and the statue
Zyzz's 'we're all gonna make it' is ironic: dying of a heart attack at 22 is not making it
Rich Piana differed from Zyzz: he openly warned people that drugs were killing him and did prevention instead of creating copycats
Zyzz encouraged kids to take clenbuterol for a six-pack, which harmed many young hearts
Zyzz shilled Jack3D, a pre-workout containing an amphetamine-like stimulant that harms the heart
Zyzz fans are almost all small, e.g. 145 lb after four years of lifting while chasing a six-pack
The aesthetic movement Zyzz started created a generation of skinny lifters obsessed with abs, some developing eating disorders and body dysmorphia
Zyzz said he couldn't cycle off because he lost muscle, so he blasted and cruised
Copycat aesthetic channels are worse role models than Zyzz because, unlike him, they lie about their drug use
Fake natties are the reason natty-or-not videos exist and why YouTube fitness declined
A 16-year-old with six months of lifting and huge arms who claims natural is lying, not a genetic outlier
Signs of a fake natural: big physique swings, long hiatuses hidden in hoodies, and sudden loss of confidence off-cycle
Real apology means stopping the behavior; fans forgive repeat liars because of parasocial attachment, like Stockholm syndrome
If someone on YouTube fitness lies to you about drugs, stop watching them
Aesthetic influencers push caffeine-heavy stimulants, programs and diets that don't work, and overpriced clothes that only look good on drug-filled frames
Same-age influencers on drugs make young fans think something is wrong with them when they can't match their physiques
Even naturally high testosterone is nowhere near cycle levels, so influencers' physiques can't be genetics
Getting big to get girls won't make you happy; promiscuous casual sex is meaningless and damages both men and women
NH regrets his own promiscuity in his early twenties
Collabs between aesthetic channels multiply their harm by exposing audiences to more bad role models
Low self-control, impatience, pleasure-seeking, promiscuity and drug use are anti-masculine traits
The aesthetic movement is 'pro bodybuilding light' and has replaced healthy natural bodybuilding
Selling supplements to a 13-year-old with promises of a drug-built physique hurts natural bodybuilding
